objects.name: Support (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
A support. Rigid: fixes the node along and about the axes of the Position's plane you choose. Elastic: a spring along or about each axis of the plane. Compression Only: holds the node only while it pushes into the support, along the plane's Z, and lets it lift - after a gap, if there is one.
Elastic and Compression Only never fix the node themselves, so a Rigid support on the same point can hold what they leave free: a pinned bearing that can lift is a Compression Only support with a Rigid one holding Tx and Ty only.
Reaction Force gives a spring support a row of its own, with the spring's force.

objects.desc: Assemble a Model

objects.name: Analysis Settings (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Collects everything OpenSees needs in order to solve - constraint handler, numberer, system of equations, convergence test, solution algorithm, integrator and stepping - into the one object Run Analysis takes.
Every input has a default, so an unconnected component already describes a valid linear static analysis. For a dynamic one set AnalysisType to Transient, and give it a Newmark or Central Difference Integrator, an Analysis Step with Dt, and a Damping.

objects.name: Run Analysis (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Writes the assembled model out as an OpenSees script, solves it, and returns the model with its results attached.
Results are recorded to a recorder.mpco file beside the Grasshopper document and read back by the 08_NumericalOutput components; an MPCO Recorder connected to Assemble Model chooses what the file holds, and what it is called. When a run fails the AlpacaModel output comes out empty - read the log output to find out why.

objects.name: Model View (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Draw the model and its results in the viewport.
Tick one or more results under Results - displacements, beam forces and stresses, shell forces and stresses, solid stresses, reactions - to draw them together, each with its own component and unit. Under Beam forces, tick any of N, Vy, Vz, T, My and Mz to draw their diagrams together. They need a model from Run Analysis or another analysis. Each element is coloured by one result: an element's own stress or force before the displacement, which colours the rest.
With none ticked, the elements are coloured by element, section or material.
Node and element ids, section names, local axes, end releases, loads and supports can be drawn over either, from the Elements, Loads and Supports menus.
ElementId shows only some of the elements and greys the rest, so what you are looking at stays in the model around it.
Geometry hands out what is drawn as coloured meshes and lines - move it, or bake it.
With Extruded on, beam stresses that differ across a section - σx, σMy, σMz, τV, τT, Von Mises - are painted point by point over it; drawn as lines, each section shows its worst.
A vibration or buckling mode is drawn at deformation scale 1 with its largest movement as far off the model as the diagrams stand; any other displacement at true size. On a natural vibration or buckling model the scale runs from -2 to 2, so Animate swings the mode both ways.

objects.name: Natural Vibration Analysis (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Solves the eigenvalue problem of the model and returns its modes, eigenvalues, periods and frequencies.
It needs no Analysis Settings - an eigenvalue problem has nothing to converge. Connect the assembled model, or an analysed one for the modes of the model it was analysed from - Section Optimiser's last design, say. Feed the solved model to Nodal Displacements to read a mode shape.
The modal report - masses, centre of mass, participation factors and mass ratios - is in the Modal Report menu below the component.

objects.name: Panel
objects.desc: A panel for custom notes and text values
objects.text:
Steel tower - a lattice tower with a stair climbing inside it.

Four tube legs, crossed bracing on every face of every storey and a landing at every level. A straight flight climbs each storey along a strip a metre wide, turning back at each landing.

The wind is typed in kN/m2: each windward leg takes it over half the tower's width, as a line load along +x. People on the stair are typed in kN/m2 too, over half the stair's width on each stringer and each beam of the landing strip. The Natural Vibration Analysis gives the tower's first six modes; the second Model View draws the first.
